sets.title: Gram panchayat election
sets.text: A gram panchayat in Thanjavur district has 12,000 registered voters. In the election, 70% of the registered voters cast their votes, and 5% of the votes cast were found invalid. Among the valid votes, Rajan got 45%, Seetha got 35% and Murali got the rest.

sets.title: A family budget in Salem
sets.text: A family in Salem has a monthly income of ₹60,000. It spends 25% of the income on rent, 20% on food, 15% on education and 10% on transport, and saves the rest. Next year the income rises by 10%, rent rises by 20%, food by 5% and education by 40%, while the transport spending stays the same. Savings are whatever remains.

sets.title: Monthly output of a Pune plant
sets.text: A two-wheeler parts factory in Pune produced 8,000 units in April. May production was 25% more than April, June production was 10% less than May, and July production was 20% more than June. The defective share of the units produced was 5% in April, 4% in May, 3% in June and 2.5% in July.

sets.title: Entrance test results
sets.text: Of the 1,200 candidates who appeared for an entrance test in Madurai, 60% were male. 45% of the male candidates and 55% of the female candidates passed the test.

sets.title: Diwali sale at an electronics store
sets.text: A store in Coimbatore offers festival discounts on the marked price: 20% on a television, 15% on a refrigerator and 12% on a washing machine. The marked prices are ₹40,000, ₹30,000 and ₹25,000 respectively. During the sale, 50 televisions, 40 refrigerators and 30 washing machines were sold. Customers paying by card got an additional 5% off the already discounted price; 30 of the televisions and 10 of the refrigerators were bought by card.

sets.title: Literacy in a district
sets.text: A district in Tamil Nadu had a population of 8,00,000 in 2015. The population grew by 10% in the five years to 2020 and by 8% in the five years from 2020 to 2025. The literacy rate (literate persons as a percentage of the population) was 72% in 2015, 78% in 2020 and 84% in 2025.

sets.title: A Bengaluru startup's three years
sets.text: A startup in Bengaluru earned a revenue of ₹50 lakh in its first year, and its expenses were 80% of the revenue. In the second year the revenue grew by 30% and the expenses grew by 20%. In the third year the revenue grew by 10% over the second year, while the expenses fell by 5% from the second year. Profit = revenue − expenses.

sets.title: Milk collection at a dairy in Anand
sets.text: A dairy in Anand collects 5,000 litres of milk in a day, of which 60% is cow milk and the rest is buffalo milk. The fat content is 3.5% in cow milk and 6.5% in buffalo milk (as a percentage of volume).

questions.questionText: How many votes were cast?
How many invalid votes were there?
How many valid votes did Rajan get?
Rajan's lead over Seetha equals what percentage of the registered voters?
questions.explanation: Lead = (45% − 35%) of 7,980 = 10% of 7,980 = 798. As a share of registered voters = 798/12,000 × 100 = 6.65%.

questions.questionText: At least how many valid votes must shift from Rajan to Seetha so that the two have exactly equal votes?
questions.explanation: Rajan leads by 798. Moving x votes from Rajan to Seetha reduces the lead by 2x, so 2x = 798 and x = 399.
questions.shortcut: Gap shifted between two people: move half the gap.

questions.questionText: What are the family's current monthly savings?
What will the monthly food expense be next year?
Next year the rent will be what percentage of the family's income (to two decimal places)?
questions.shortcut: Rent grows faster than income, so its share must exceed 25%.

questions.questionText: What will the monthly savings be next year?
questions.explanation: New spends: rent 18,000, food 12,600, education 9,000 × 1.4 = 12,600, transport 6,000; total = 49,200. Savings = 66,000 − 49,200 = ₹16,800.

questions.questionText: By what percentage (to two decimal places) will the savings fall next year?
questions.explanation: Fall = 18,000 − 16,800 = ₹1,200. Percentage fall = 1,200/18,000 × 100 = 6.67%. Income rose 10% but savings fell, because spending rose faster.
questions.shortcut: Always take the percentage change on the old savings, not the new.

questions.questionText: How many units did the factory produce in June?
How many defective units were produced in July?
How many non-defective units were produced in July?
questions.explanation: July production = 10,800 and defective = 270, so good units = 10,800 − 270 = 10,530.

questions.questionText: Over the four months together, the defective units form what percentage of total production (nearest 0.1%)?
By what percentage (nearest 0.1%) were the good units in July higher than the good units in April?
questions.explanation: April good units = 8,000 − 400 = 7,600. July good units = 10,530. Rise = 2,930, and 2,930/7,600 × 100 = 38.55%, i.e. 38.6%. (Using total production instead gives 35%, which is the trap.)

questions.questionText: How many female candidates appeared for the test?
How many male candidates passed?
What is the overall pass percentage?
Female candidates form what percentage of all those who passed (nearest 0.1%)?
questions.explanation: Female passers = 264 and total passers = 588. Share = 264/588 × 100 = 44.90%, i.e. 44.9%.

questions.questionText: How many more candidates would have to pass for the overall pass percentage to become 55%?
questions.explanation: 55% of 1,200 = 660. Currently 588 passed, so 660 − 588 = 72 more must pass.

questions.questionText: What is the selling price of a television after the festival discount?
What is the selling price of a washing machine after the festival discount?
What is the total sales revenue at the festival-discounted prices (before any card discount)?
The overall discount given, as a percentage of the total marked value, is closest to which value?
After the extra card discount, what is the total revenue of the store?
What was the population in 2020?
How many people were literate in 2015?
What was the population in 2025?
questions.explanation: 2025 population = 8,80,000 × 1.08 = 9,50,400. (Not 18% over 2015, because the 8% applies to the 2020 base.)

questions.questionText: How many people were literate in 2025?
The number of literate persons in 2025 was what percentage more than in 2015?
questions.explanation: Increase = 7,98,336 − 5,76,000 = 2,22,336. Percentage = 2,22,336/5,76,000 × 100 = 38.6%. The rise is larger than the literacy-rate rise (12 points) because the population also grew.

questions.questionText: What was the profit in the first year?
What was the revenue in the second year?
In the second year, the profit was what percentage of the revenue (nearest 0.01%)?
questions.explanation: Expenses = 40 × 1.2 = 48 lakh. Profit = 65 − 48 = 17 lakh. Profit margin = 17/65 × 100 = 26.15%.

questions.questionText: What were the expenses in the third year?
questions.explanation: Expenses in year 2 = 48 lakh. Year 3 = 48 × 0.95 = ₹45.6 lakh.

questions.questionText: The third-year profit was what percentage higher than the first-year profit?
questions.explanation: Revenue year 3 = 65 × 1.1 = 71.5 lakh. Profit = 71.5 − 45.6 = 25.9 lakh. Increase over 10 lakh = 15.9 lakh, i.e. 15.9/10 × 100 = 159%.
questions.shortcut: Percentage increase uses the old value as the base: 25.9/10 = 259% of the old, i.e. 159% more.

questions.questionText: How many litres of cow milk does the dairy collect?
How many litres of fat are there in the buffalo milk collected?
questions.explanation: Buffalo milk = 40% of 5,000 = 2,000 litres. Fat = 6.5% of 2,000 = 130 litres.

questions.questionText: What is the average fat percentage of the mixed milk?
If 500 litres of water is added to the mixed milk, the fat percentage becomes (nearest 0.01%)
questions.explanation: Fat stays at 235 L but volume becomes 5,500 L. Fat % = 235/5,500 × 100 = 4.27%.

questions.questionText: How many litres of pure buffalo milk must be added to the original 5,000 litres to raise the average fat content to exactly 5%?
questions.shortcut: Alligation: 6.5 − 5 = 1.5 parts vs 5 − 4.7 = 0.3 parts, so 5,000 : x = 1.5 : 0.3.
